A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DUNIA and provide readable main texts, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval, fine-tuning and waveform-generation results across seven Earth-observation tasks, alongside architectural ablations and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds comparator evaluations, runtime measurements, temporal tests and input-sensitivity experiments.

M1.justification: The dual-decoder architecture, waveform and multitemporal autoencoders, Zero-CL/VICReg alignment, reconstruction losses and diffusion generator remain unchanged. Matching the appendices confirms that expanded architectural explanations do not introduce new method components; the fine-tuning revisions concern evaluation settings.

E1.justification: The seven tasks and core French datasets are retained. Appendix H adds cross-year evaluation for 2019 and 2021, pooled 2019–2021 pretraining, single-sensor inputs and single-date imagery scenarios. These extend temporal and input-condition coverage within the existing domains.

E2.justification: Fine-tuning comparisons expand from AnySat and CROMA to include DOFA, DeCUR and SatMAE in Tables 2 and G2. Table 1 also adds canopy-height comparisons with Liu et al. (2023), Tolan et al. (2024) and Lang et al. (2023), alongside Schwartz et al. (2023). These are reported comparisons, not merely new citations.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes comparator pretraining from 200K to 250K steps and DUNIA fine-tuning from the last two neighborhood-attention layers to the last layer. Added protocols vary input size, retrieval database size, neighbor count and temporal training/evaluation design. These reported revisions do not establish that retained results were rerun. Table G2 also changes the PASTIS sample count from 300 to 300K images, an unexplained inconsistency with the stated dataset size.

E4.justification: The five original ablations are retained as H.1–H.5. New sections H.6–H.10 examine retrieval overhead, input-size sensitivity, temporal stability, sensor contributions and median composites versus single-date inputs. Appendix D adds a t-SNE comparison of pixel and patch embeddings, and Appendix I expands qualitative map examples.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added evaluations continue to report point estimates without introducing uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial comparator and supplementary results. For example, Table H11 reports PASTIS wF1 of 42.3 with single-date inputs versus 77.0 with median composites; Table H6 reports DUNIA runtimes of 4.22/4.80 seconds versus 177.37 for AnySat. Existing principal DUNIA table values are retained or rounded, while smaller-data results move to Appendix G; these do not demonstrate new same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The alignment losses, diffusion formulations and radar-normalization equation are retained after appendix relocation and equation renumbering. The decoder-channel index correction in Section 3.1 agrees with the formula already present in v1 Appendix A.1. No substantive mathematical assumptions, derivations or proofs are added.

C1.justification: Both versions claim pixel-level horizontal/vertical alignment, effective retrieval across seven tasks, competitive fine-tuning on five of six tasks and waveform generation from pixel embeddings. Rewording and additional supporting experiments do not materially redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 explicitly qualifies median composites as more informative than single-date images but less informative than full time series. H.10 attributes their advantage to more stable, representative reflectance patterns. These refine the temporal-information interpretation; the existing limitations concerning static inputs and geographic/year specificity remain.

D1.justification: Section 4 adds a code-repository link absent from v1, and Table G1 explicitly lists the selected neighbor count for each task. Most architecture, optimizer, hardware and diffusion settings are carried over from v1 Appendix D to v2 Appendix E.

R1.justification: A dedicated Section 2.2 substantially expands domain-specific positioning by discussing masked-reconstruction and contrastive approaches for Earth observation, including SatMAE, SatMAE++, DOFA, CROMA, DeCUR and AnySat. Additional canopy-height literature also broadens the context beyond v1's primarily general contrastive and multimodal review.

P1.justification: Section 3 receives a rewritten, multi-paragraph architectural overview, and related work gains a dedicated EO subsection. Existing appendix material is substantially reorganized: objectives and waveform generation become separate sections, experimental settings move, and reduced-label evaluations receive their own section. Terminology and prose are also edited throughout.

P2.justification: Figure 2 becomes a simplified architecture diagram while the detailed diagram moves to Figure A1. v2 adds Figure D1 and Tables H6–H11, restructures Tables 1–2 with smaller-data results in G1–G2, and expands the original combined map figure into Figures I1–I3. The four waveform-example figures remain unchanged apart from presentation and numbering.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens comparative validation and the justification of practical design choices through broader baselines and targeted temporal, sensor, compositing and runtime tests. Clearer architectural diagrams and code-access information also improve usability. Table G2's inconsistent PASTIS count and unexplained setting revisions limit reproducibility, but these localized problems do not outweigh the substantial gains in evidence and explanation.
